What you did wasn’t so bad.

You stood in a small room, waiting for the sun.

At least you told yourself that.

I know it was small,

but there was something, a kind of pulped lemon,

at the low edge of the sky.

 

No, you’re right, it was terrible.

Terrible to live without love

in small rooms with vinyl blinds

listening to music secretly,

the secret music of one’s head

which can’t be shared.

 

A dream is the only way to breathe.

But you must

find a more useful way to live.

I suppose you’re right

this was a failure: to stand there

so still, waiting for—what?

 

When I think about this life,

the life you led, I think of England,

of secret gardens that never open,

and novels sliding off the bed

at night where the small handkerchief

of darkness settles over

one’s face.

 

Source

The trick is to never wait still. Our lives are cyclical: we can't help but wake up in our bed at morning and go to sleep on it again at night and repeat that every day (or most days). Few of us live a different lifestyle. But if we manage to make any sort of progress each day, no matter how small, it will turn this cycle into a spiral, growing with each day and eventually gaining momentum as months and years pass by. This is how I try to live my life. It may sound like "failure" if you look at the day-to-day movement but looking back I have much to pride myself for and hope for much more when I think of the future.
